title: "Working With cancensus"
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  eval = identical(Sys.getenv("IN_PKGDOWN"), "true") &&
    (nzchar(Sys.getenv("CM_API_KEY")) ||
      nzchar(Sys.getenv("CANCENSUS_API_KEY")))
)
```

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(griddy)
library(dplyr)
```

This article runs the core `griddy` workflow on census tracts in the City of
Vancouver, using median total household income from the 2016 and 2021
censuses (incomes for 2015 and 2020). It needs a CensusMapper API key. It
renders on the pkgdown site when one is set and does not ship with the
package.

```{r, results='hide', fig.alt=c("Heatmap of Canadian Census tract transition probabilities between income quintiles.", "Faceted heatmaps of Canadian Census tract spatial Markov transition probabilities by spatial-lag quintile.")}
library(cancensus)
library(sf)
library(sfdep)

regions <- list(CSD = "5915022") # Vancouver CSD
vectors <- c(
  income_2016 = "v_CA16_2397",
  income_2021 = "v_CA21_906"
)

panel_2016 <- get_census(
  dataset = "CA16",
  regions = regions,
  vectors = vectors["income_2016"],
  level = "CT",
  geo_format = "sf"
) |>
  transmute(GeoUID, year = 2016L, median_income = income_2016, geometry)

panel_2021 <- get_census(
  dataset = "CA21",
  regions = regions,
  vectors = vectors["income_2021"],
  level = "CT",
  geo_format = "sf"
) |>
  transmute(GeoUID, year = 2021L, median_income = income_2021, geometry)

common_ids <- intersect(panel_2016$GeoUID, panel_2021$GeoUID)
panel <- bind_rows(panel_2016, panel_2021) |>
  filter(GeoUID %in% common_ids)
geography <- panel |>
  filter(year == 2021L) |>
  arrange(GeoUID) |>
  mutate(
    nb = st_contiguity(geometry, queen = TRUE),
    wt = st_weights(nb, allow_zero = TRUE)
  )

classes <- classify_dynamics(panel, GeoUID, year, median_income, k = 5)
classic <- markov_dynamics(classes, GeoUID, year, class)
spatial <- spatial_markov(panel, GeoUID, year, median_income, geometry = geography, k = 5)

plot_transition_matrix(classic)
plot_spatial_markov(spatial)
```

## Reading the output

With two censuses, each tract contributes exactly one transition, from 2016
to 2021. The first plot is the transition matrix over those moves. The second
splits them by the income class of each tract's neighbors in 2016. With one
transition per tract, the conditional matrices rest on few observations, so
treat them as an illustration.

## Before using this for analysis

- **Incomes are nominal.** 2015 and 2020 incomes are not adjusted for
  inflation, so pooled classes mix shared growth with relative movement.
  Divide each census's incomes by their median before classifying to study
  relative movement.
- **Tract boundaries change between censuses.** Matching on `GeoUID` keeps
  tracts whose identifier persisted, but a persisting identifier does not
  guarantee an unchanged boundary. The
  [`tongfen`](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=tongfen) package builds a
  common geography across census years.
